proposals.evidence: Platts p. 295 gives Persian piyāz “onion”; the visually checked Hindi table has प्याज, independently supporting the existing Hindi pyaj donor. Survey piaj/pjaj and z/j/s adaptations belong to this regional loan family. The borrowed edge identifies a provisional Hindi/Urdu route; it does not assert direct Persian contact for each target. Existing Hindi pyaj “onion” is the provisional donor, under the user’s preference to link supported cross-IA families. An intermediate Indo-Aryan language or another lending locality remains possible; the attestation locality is not claimed as the historical lending site.
